qualitative.3m: Lab automation software and OEM diagnostics components have switching costs, but low pricing power in OEM contract manufacturing (Paramit) and cyclical lab instrument capex depress multi-year ROIC to ~7-8% (and negative with 2025 impairment), failing the 12% hurdle.

qualitative.3m: Massive scale in Medicaid and ACA marketplace administration (~28M members, ~$195B revenue) provides provider network contracting advantages, but returns are structurally bounded by government-mandated reimbursement rates, statutory minimum medical loss ratio floors (85%), and acute exposure to medical cost trend shocks.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & zero autonomous pricing power, REJECT). Centene operates as a massive scale government-sponsored managed care contractor, but structural returns on capital hover at 3-8% (10Y median 8.5%), failing the 12% hurdle. Premiums are set administratively by state Medicaid agencies and CMS, leaving margins vulnerable to medical inflation, utilization spikes, and post-redetermination acuity mismatches.
qualitative.evidence: Centene generates ~$195B in top-line revenue but operates at razor-thin margins (~1.9% operating margin in 2023-2024, swinging into operating losses in Medicaid segments post-redeterminations). Structural 10-year GAAP ROIC averages 8.5%, falling short of the 12% threshold.

qualitative.3m: Possesses significant regional scale advantages as the largest Blue Cross Blue Shield licensee (operating across 14 states with ~46M members) and vertical capabilities via Carelon. However, it lacks genuine unconstrained pricing power: statutory ACA minimum Medical Loss Ratios (80/85%) act as a regulatory cap on underwriting profitability, over 50% of revenue is tied to government reimbursement (Medicaid capitation and CMS Medicare Advantage benchmark rates), and medical cost surges (GLP-1 specialty pharmacy, elevated surgical utilization) cannot be dynamically passed through without rate approval delays and commercial membership attrition.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Major US managed care organization operating Blue Cross Blue Shield plans across 14 states alongside Carelon health services. While network scale and local provider density provide meaningful cost advantages, the business lacks true pricing power >= inflation due to statutory ACA 80/85% medical loss ratio caps, state Medicaid reimbursement rate lags following redeterminations, and CMS Medicare Advantage rate determinations. Medical utilization and pharmacy cost spikes surge MLR (benefit expense ratio reached 90.0% in FY2025 and 93.5% in Q4 2025) and cannot be passed through immediately without driving customer churn.
qualitative.evidence: Elevance generates over $170B in revenue serving ~46M medical members. Benefit expense ratio escalated from 87.0% in 2023 to 88.5% in 2024 and 90.0% in FY2025, peaking at 93.5% in Q4 2025. Inability to dynamically adjust commercial and Medicaid rates to offset surgical utilization and GLP-1 specialty pharmacy spikes led to significant earnings compression, demonstrating the structural absence of pricing power above inflation.

qualitative.3m: Scale economies shared in Medicare Advantage membership and CenterWell senior clinics provide operational efficiency, but fail to produce economic moats. 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 11.2% falls short of the 12% hurdle, while acute exposure to CMS regulatory payment benchmarks and Star Ratings cuts completely disproves pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Humana lacks autonomous pricing power as Medicare Advantage benchmark rates are determined administratively by CMS. CMS Star Ratings downgrades and higher medical utilization (benefit ratio surged to ~90%) crushed operating earnings, while multi-cycle GAAP ROIC of 11.2% fails the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Over 80% of revenue is tied to Medicare Advantage. Operating margins dropped to <2% in 2024-2025 as CMS risk-adjustment cuts (v28 phase-in) and elevated inpatient utilization coincided with a sharp reduction in Star Ratings bonus payments.

qualitative.3m: UnitedHealth Group commands unmatched operational scale across health benefits (UnitedHealthcare) and integrated care/PBM services (Optum), negotiating deep provider discounts and prescription rebates. However, it fails the empirical moat test on pricing power and returns on capital. Crucially, pricing power is constrained by CMS statutory payment rates in Medicare Advantage (effective net rate cuts in 2024-2026 under the v28 risk adjustment model) amidst elevated medical cost inflation and utilization surges, pushing the medical care ratio (MCR) to 88.9% in 2025. When management re-architected plan benefits and raised premiums to recover margins, it suffered severe customer churn, shedding over 1.0 million Medicare Advantage members. Furthermore, strict NOPAT ROIC collapsed to 9.5% in 2024 and 7.9% in 2025 (failing the >=12.0% hurdle), while OptumRx faces bipartisan legislative and FTC scrutiny threatening historical PBM spread pricing.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). UnitedHealth Group lacks pricing power above inflation due to statutory CMS Medicare Advantage payment caps, elevated post-pandemic healthcare utilization (medical care ratio expanded to 88.9% in 2025), and customer churn (>1M MA members shed upon benefit adjustments). Strict GAAP NOPAT ROIC collapsed to 7.9% in 2025, falling well below the 12% hurdle. Expanding DOJ antitrust scrutiny targeting UnitedHealthcare/Optum vertical ties, forced Amedisys divestitures, and legislative PBM spread-pricing reform compound terminal headwinds.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle Financial Performance: Revenues expanded from $257.1B in FY2020 to $400.3B in FY2024 and $447.6B in FY2025. GAAP Net Income was $14.41B in 2024 and $12.06B in 2025, down from a peak of $22.38B in 2023. Strict GAAP NOPAT ROIC dropped to 9.54% in 2024 and 7.90% in 2025, falling below the mandatory >=12.0% capital efficiency threshold as invested capital expanded ($197.6B in 2025) following acquisitions while operating earnings compressed. In 2024-2025, MCR escalated to 88.9% in 2025. When management attempted to restore margins by curtailing supplemental benefits and raising premiums, the company suffered substantial member churn, forfeiting over 1.0 million MA enrollees.

qualitative.3m: Merck's economic moat is grounded in proprietary patent estates, regulatory exclusivity, and biologic manufacturing know-how, centered on its blockbuster oncology PD-1 therapy Keytruda (pembrolizumab, $31.64B revenue in FY25), HPV vaccine Gardasil, and newer launches Winrevair and Capvaxive. While these high-margin assets deliver 74-76% gross margins and high historical returns on capital (5-year median GAAP ROIC of ~18-21%), Merck structurally lacks demonstrated pricing power >= inflation across the full drug cycle. Branded prescription drugs face pervasive state price caps and statutory payor restrictions: under the US Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), price increases exceeding CPI-U trigger mandatory 100% inflation rebate penalties, and Keytruda is scheduled for direct Medicare price negotiation starting in 2028. European and global single-payer systems mandate regular price cuts, while Gardasil demonstrated severe volume vulnerability in China (-39% sales drop in FY25 to $5.23B). Furthermore, the primary US composition-of-matter patent protecting IV Keytruda expires in December 2028, leading to inevitable 80-90% biosimilar price erosion rather than enduring pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). While Merck maintains high current returns on capital via patent-protected blockbuster Keytruda ($31.64B in FY25, ~48% of total revenue) and Gardasil, the business model lacks demonstrated pricing power >= inflation across the cycle. Branded prescription drugs operate under statutory price caps and regulatory constraints: the US Inflation Reduction Act legally penalizes price hikes above CPI via mandatory rebates and mandates direct Medicare price negotiations starting in 2028 for Keytruda. International markets impose statutory price cuts, and Gardasil sales in China dropped 39% in FY25 under competitive/procurement pressure. With Keytruda's primary US patent expiring in December 2028, pricing power is strictly temporary rather than enduring, leading to unavoidable biosimilar price deflation.
qualitative.evidence: Keytruda generates ~$31.6B (~48% of Merck's total revenue). Primary US patent expires in late 2028. Under IRA rules, Keytruda will enter direct price negotiations in 2028, capping lifetime returns. Gardasil sales dropped 39% in China due to domestic competition, proving vulnerability to international tender dynamics.

qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Asset-light third-party freight brokerage operating in a fragmented, highly competitive market with no customer switching costs or pricing power. Gross margins fluctuate with spot truckload freight rates.
qualitative.evidence: Reported ROIC is optically elevated (~22%) due to zero tangible asset base, but gross profits swing violently with spot truckload cycle. Shippers switch brokers electronically with zero friction.

Intermediates cargo capacity between shippers and carriers with proprietary IT systems and customized regulatory customs compliance where failure halts shipments. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 50.6% and operating ROIC >50% prove pricing power.

qualitative.3m: Global express hub-and-spoke air network (Memphis World Hub, 680+ aircraft) and sorting infrastructure are virtually impossible to replicate from scratch, but fail to deliver excess economic returns. Heavy capital intensity, chronic capacity overexpansion, and aggressive pricing competition from UPS and Amazon Logistics suppress multi-cycle GAAP ROIC to ~7-8%, well below the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). While FedEx operates an irreplaceable global air express and ground logistics network, heavy capital intensity ($4B-$6B+ annual capex for aircraft, hubs, and vehicle fleet) and competitive pressure from UPS and Amazon keep operating margins at 5.5-7.0% and multi-cycle ROIC at 7-8%, well below the 12% threshold.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.5% (consistently failing 12% hurdle). Capital expenditures consume 6-8% of revenue annually. Lost the USPS primary air cargo contract to UPS in 2024, demonstrating price competition in parcel transport.

qualitative.3m: UPS operates massive physical route density and integrated hub-and-spoke sortation networks with enterprise B2B pickup lock-in. However, the moat suffers severe structural erosion: it lacks pricing power above inflation without shedding customer volume and market share. The 2023 Teamsters labor contract created a structural cost disadvantage against non-union rivals, while Amazon Logistics successfully insourced and disintermediated delivery, stripping away high-density volume. Shippers actively divert volume to FedEx, USPS, and regional carriers upon aggressive price hikes.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). UPS operates an indispensable physical parcel network, but it lacks genuine pricing power above inflation without shedding customer volume and market share. The landmark 2023 Teamsters labor agreement significantly escalated union wage and benefit costs, causing margin compression that could not be passed through to price-sensitive customers. Furthermore, Amazon Logistics has permanently disintermediated UPS's former largest customer (shedding over 50% of Amazon volume), while commercial shippers diverted volume to FedEx and regional carriers, depressing operating margins (~8%) and dropping normalized ROIC toward ~11-13% with sub-hurdle incremental ROIIC.
qualitative.evidence: Historical ROIC was elevated during the 2020-2022 pandemic e-commerce boom, but normalized post-pandemic operating margins compressed to ~7-8%. Teamsters labor contract added billions in wage/benefit inflation, while package volume declined as commercial shippers diverted freight to non-union carriers.

qualitative.3m: DHL Express possesses an elite global air hub-and-spoke network with significant scale economies shared and high TDI margins. However, consolidated group pricing power is severely impaired by Post & Parcel Germany, which is subject to statutory price caps by the German Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) and inflexible unionized labor costs, alongside the commoditized price-taker nature of Global Forwarding.
qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat). While DHL Express is a world-class global air express oligopolist with FedEx and UPS, the consolidated group remains burdened by Post & Parcel Germany, where statutory postal price caps from BNetzA and heavy collective bargaining wage settlements prevent inflation pass-through, while Global Forwarding operates as a cyclical freight rate price-taker.
qualitative.evidence: Group multi-year ROIC averages ~11.9% (failing 12% hurdle). Post & Parcel Germany is legally restricted by BNetzA from raising regulated postage rates to match double-digit domestic wage inflation, while freight forwarding spreads normalized downwards.

qualitative.3m: DSV is a best-in-class logistics consolidator with an unmatched M&A integration engine and asset-light scale economies shared. However, air and ocean forwarding remains an intermediary brokerage business where enterprise shippers multi-source and tender volume regularly with low switching costs, leaving DSV unable to exert autonomous pricing power >= inflation across the cycle without losing volume.
qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat). Although DSV possesses an exceptional acquisition integration playbook (crowned by the €14.3B DB Schenker transaction) and attractive asset-light capital efficiency, freight forwarding lacks structural switching costs. Shippers regularly tender routes on price, making DSV a price-taker on freight spreads without autonomous pricing power >= inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Reported pre-tax ROIC including goodwill ranges from 15% to 25%, but EBIT declined ~36% between 2022 and 2024 as pandemic-era freight premiums evaporated. Freight forwarding contracts are tendered annually or bi-annually, proving shippers treat forwarding as a competitive service.
